title: Rational Immigration Policy in an Irrational Age
what_it_is: Rational Immigration Policy in an Irrational Age

sections.label: American schools Arabic numerals poll
sections.summary: Asked whether American schools should teach Arabic numerals, 56% of over 2,000 respondents said no.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The question was, "Should schools in America teach Arabic numerals as part of their curriculum?" Fifty-six percent, or more than 2,000 respondents, said "No".

sections.label: Immigrant number misperceptions
sections.summary: Respondents in six countries think immigrant numbers are two to three times larger than they are.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The average respondent in these six countries thinks that the number of immigrants is about two to three times larger than it is in fact.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, Americans think that more than one in three people in the US is an immigrant.

sections.label: MOM Singapore Citizens Labour Force report
sections.summary: MOM's January report found little difference between resident and citizen outcomes, as citizens are 85% of the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOM released the report "Singapore Citizens in the Labour Force" in January to address these concerns.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Minister Teo explained, there is actually little difference for many indicators between overall resident outcomes and citizen outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is because citizens form 85% of our labour force.

sections.label: Estimated PR and citizen employment rates
sections.summary: Estimated PR employment rate rose from about 70% to 74%, versus 60% to 63% for citizens.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Using this principle and some assumptions, I have computed estimated labour market outcomes for permanent residents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I estimate the PR employment rate rose from about 70% to 74% over the last decade, compared to a rise from about 60% to 63% for citizens.

sections.label: PMET share among employed citizens
sections.summary: The share of PMETs among employed citizens rose from about 47% in 2009 to 54% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In contrast, the share of PMETs among employed citizens rose from about 47% in 2009 to 54% in 2018.

sections.label: Estimated PR and citizen earnings gap
sections.summary: Assuming similar wage distribution, a rough estimate is that PRs earn about 35% more than citizens.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, if you assume the wage distribution is similar, a rough estimate is that PRs earn about 35% more than citizens do.

sections.label: PR retrenchment rate higher
sections.summary: The estimated retrenchment rate for PRs is much higher than that for citizens.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The estimated retrenchment rate for PRs is actually much higher than that for citizens.

sections.label: IPS paper on immigration support
sections.summary: A 2019 Institute of Policy Studies paper found Singaporeans broadly supported immigration benefits but preferred immigration below 20% of the population.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2019 Institute of Policy Studies paper by Mathews, Tay and Selvarajan found that Singaporeans expressed broad support for the benefits of immigration, but they did prefer a calibrated level of immigration at below 20% of the population.

sections.label: Publishing PR labour market facts
sections.summary: A researcher should not need to estimate PR labour market outcomes when they could be published outright, requiring courage to accept political risk.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There really should not be a need for a researcher to estimate what are the labour market outcomes of PRs, when it would be easy to publish them outright.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must have courage to accept the political risk of publishing facts on immigration that may be uncomfortable, but are nonetheless better than pleasant platitudes.

sections.label: Alternative narrative on immigration
sections.summary: An alternative narrative should stress building a common future, treating immigrants as contributors and partners, with fact- and research-based immigration policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should not be surprised, then, if the immigrants we attract with this mindset likewise think of Singapore as a means and not as an end.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must build an alternative narrative that stresses building a common future together, not preserving a comfortable past.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But to retain our vibrancy and relevance we must move forward as a country that treats immigrants as potential contributors and partners in developing the Singapore of tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need an immigration policy that allows the Singapore – and Singaporeans – of tomorrow to be a better version of who we are today.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With a fact- and research-based approach to immigration policy, education and engagement of Singaporeans and an outstretched hand to immigrants who want to join us in this journey, I believe we can build on today's Singapore for a better tomorrow.

sections.label: Calibrated immigrant flow and integration
sections.summary: A stable, calibrated flow of new immigrants moderates ageing and shrinking citizen population, prioritising those who integrate and sink roots.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is essential to keep our society strong and our economy vibrant, both of which are important foundations to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We take in a stable and calibrated flow of new immigrants to moderate the impact of an ageing citizen population and prevent it from shrinking over time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Rather, we want to build a strong and resilient Singapore, with a distinct sense of national identity and common destiny.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We, therefore, prioritise new immigrants with the ability to integrate well into our society, and who have expressed their commitment to sinking roots here.

sections.label: New citizens from PRs
sections.summary: New citizens are drawn from the pool of PRs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Keep in mind that we draw new citizens from the pool of PRs.

sections.label: PR and citizenship applications
sections.summary: Applications for PR and citizenship each year far exceed the number of places granted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Every year, the number of applications for PR and citizenship far exceed the number of places that we grant.
